bull.b: Quarterly revenue and production growth, combined with stable reservoir pressure and little to no decline in producing wells, indicates the existing asset base is generating operational traction. If sustained, these improvements can support throughput and revenue without relying solely on new field acquisitions.

Completed Hondo reconstruction, upgraded controls and safety systems, and planned perforations targeting roughly 2,400 additional barrels per day create a defined route to higher output. Expanding midstream capacity also supports processing platform production and reducing operational bottlenecks.

TTM revenue rose 111.5% to $292.8 million and EBITDA was positive at $24.3 million, showing that restored production can produce operating-level earnings capacity even before full profitability. Sustaining this rebound would improve the platform for absorbing fixed offshore costs.

bear.b: Although revenue has rebounded sharply, negative gross profit and a $592.7 million TTM net loss show that scale has not translated into economically profitable operations. Persistent annual losses and heavily negative operating profit make earnings quality fragile if production gains do not improve unit economics.

TTM operating cash flow of -$244.9 million and free cash flow of -$391.9 million indicate the business is not self-funding. Continued annual cash deficits, together with a 29.9% decline in free cash flow versus the prior period, can constrain investment and increase reliance on outside capital.

Debt of about $960.2 million against $324.3 million of equity creates a pressured capital structure, while equity fell from $534.3 million to $324.3 million. This combination reduces financial flexibility, increases dependence on debt-supported operations, and leaves less cushion against setbacks.
